chunks: 5016 - And Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū Maryam, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

A woman came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said, “Indeed, I have committed adultery.” So he turned his face away from her. Then she moved until she faced him and said, “Indeed, I have committed adultery,” but he turned his face away from her. Then she faced him again and said, “Indeed, I have committed adultery,” so he turned away from her. Then she faced him again and said, “Indeed, I have committed adultery,” so he ordered concerning her and she was detained. She was pregnant, so he waited for her until she gave birth.

Then after that he gave orders concerning her, and a pit was dug for her in al-Raḥabah. He stitched a new garment upon her and placed her in the pit up to the waist and the place of the breasts, and he closed the gate of al-Raḥabah and cast a stone at her and said, “In the Name of Allah. O Allah, upon affirming Your Book and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet.”

Then he ordered Qanbar, and he cast a stone at her. Then he entered his house and said, “O Qanbar, permit the companions of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله to enter.” So they entered and stoned her, each with a stone. Then they stood not knowing whether they should return to their stones or stone with other than them, while there was still life in her. So they said, “O Qanbar, inform him that we have stoned her with our stones and there is still life in her, so what should we do?” He said, “Return to your stones.” So they returned until she died.
Then they said to him, “She has died, so what should we do with her?” He said, “Then deliver her to her relatives and instruct them to do with her as they do with their dead.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهَا: Her relatives/guardians; those to whom her body was to be returned after death.
key_terms.الرَّحَبَةِ: Al-Raḥabah; the open space where the punishment was carried out.
key_terms.تَصْدِيقِ كِتَابِكَ: Affirming Your Book; expressing conformity with the divine command.
key_terms.حَامِلًا: Pregnant; indicating the delay of punishment until after childbirth.
key_terms.حَفِيرَةٌ: A pit dug for carrying out the stoning.
key_terms.رَمَقٌ: A remaining trace of life; indicating that she was still alive during the process.
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ: The sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet; acting in accordance with prophetic practice.
key_terms.فَجَرْتُ: I committed adultery/fornication; the woman’s self-confession to illicit sexual intercourse.

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام implement the legal punishment for a pregnant woman who repeatedly confessed to adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the case of a woman who repeatedly confessed to adultery before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, after which the legal punishment was carried out only after her pregnancy had ended. It also records procedural details of the implementation of rajm and shows that, after death, her body was to be returned to her family for the usual rites given to the deceased.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5016 - Yunus ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Maryam, who narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that a woman came to Commander of the Faithful (as) and said: "I have committed adultery."

Imam (as) turned his face away from her.
She moved to face Imam (as) again and repeated: "I have committed adultery," but Imam (as) turned away once more.
She repeated it a third and then a fourth time.
After the fourth confession, Imam (as) ordered that she be detained.
It was discovered that she was pregnant, so Imam (as) waited until she gave birth.

Afterward, Imam (as) commanded that a pit be dug for her in the open space of Rahbah.
Imam (as) dressed her in a new garment and placed her into the pit up to her waist and chest level.
Imam (as) then closed the gate of Rahbah and threw a stone at her, saying, "In the name of Allah (swt). O' Allah (swt), in confirmation of Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet."

Then Imam (as) instructed Qanbar to throw a stone at her. Afterward, Imam (as) returned to his house and said: "O' Qanbar, permit the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to enter."
They entered and began stoning her, each throwing a stone. When they were unsure whether to reuse the same stones or throw new ones while she was still alive, they said: "O' Qanbar, inform him that we have stoned her with our stones, but she is still alive. What should we do?"
Imam (as) replied: "Return to your stones," and they continued until she died.

They asked: "She has now died, what should we do with her?"
Imam (as) said: "Hand her over to her family and instruct them to treat her as they would their deceased."
